slides.title: Anthropic New Billing June 15 Anthropic New Billing
slides.text: Anthropic New Billing June 15 Anthropic New Billing June 15 Splitting Claude's subscription into two separate usage pools: one for interactive chat - continues as before one for agentic usage - calculated at API rate https://beam.ai/agentic-insights/anthropics-new-billing-split-reveals-what-ai-agents-actually-cost When you have monthly subscription of $X/month, you get $X in credits for agentic use at full API rates. After using these credits, you will be automatically billed extra at API rate (if you enabled "extra usage") - or requests simply halt once the monthly credit is exhausted This affects: claude -p (run one prompt - and exit) Claude Agent SDK (Python and TypeScript) Claude Code GitHub Actions Third-party apps using Agent SDK authentication (OpenClaw, Zed's Claude integration, Conductor, Jean, ...) Interactive CLI sessions in terminal (or interactive session in Claude desktop app) are not affected - they will continue to draw from your standard subscription pool, just as before; So if you use "claude" command in terminal for interactive session - it is still billed as part of your monthly subscription. You can ask it to do multi-step operation (long task list) - still billed through subscription. Careful - remove your ANTHROPIC_API_KEY key, because when you hit your subscription's 5-hour limit, Claude Code may automatically switch to using that API key instead Unused credits do not roll over - they expire at the end of each billing cycle; Credits are "per-user" and cannot be pooled or transferred across team members Zed Claude Agent, VSCode Claude Code Extension, PyCharm (JetBrains) Claude Code Plugin - billing depends on task Interactive question - can be billed through monthly subscription Agentic tasks (autonomous file edits, multi-step coding runs, anything using the Agent SDK under the hood) - counts against your new credit pool after June 15 Model Type Cost per 1Mtok in/out - or Mem Agentic Strength Claude Opus 4.8 Cloud $15/$75 Best Gemini 3.1 Pro Cloud $2/$12 Frontier, 1M context, multimodal Qwen3-235B-A22B Local 130GB RAM Near-frontier, excellent tool calling Kimi K2.5 Cloud $0.45 / $2.25 Top general agentic, complex tool use, long sessions Qwen3 Coder 480B A35B Cloud $0.40 / $1.60 Best-in-class for coding agents specifically GPT-4.1 Mini Cloud $0.40 / $1.60 Strong tool calling, 1M context, solid coding Llama 3.3 70B Local ~40GB RAM Strong generalist agent, widely supported in Ollama DeepSeek-V3-0324 Cloud $0.20 / $0.77 Excellent cost/performance, strong coding agents Qwen3.6‑35B‑A3B (MoE) Local ~22GB RAM Great reasoning + tool calling, tiny active params Qwen3 Coder 30B-A3B Local ~18GB RAM Same MoE efficiency, tuned for code GLM-4.5-Air Local ~20GB RAM Purpose-built for agents, MoE architecture Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite Cloud $0.25 / $1.50 Good tool use, very fast, lowest cloud cost Qwen 3.7 Plus Cloud $0.40 / $1.60 Multimodal Agent-focused So we can still use Claude Subscription for coding if we use Claude Code CLI To run "digital employee" we can select cheaper models:

slides.title: AI Updates How to contain Claude across products
slides.text: AI Updates How to contain Claude across products - Anthropic post https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/how-we-contain-claude How to limit the "blast radius" when Claude makes mistakes across claude.ai, Claude Code, and Claude Cowork They use layered containment: sandboxed environments, OS-level restrictions, and isolated VMs Each product is scoped differently: claude.ai runs in ephemeral server containers Claude Code uses OS sandboxing with human oversight Claude Cowork runs full VMs with strict egress controls They share real security incidents - including a prompt injection that exfiltrated AWS credentials 24 out of 25 times - to illustrate why deterministic environment-level controls matter more than probabilistic model-layer defenses Key emerging concerns include memory poisoning, multi-agent trust escalation, and agent identity management DeepSWE AI coding benchmark by data-curve.ai Designed to mimic real-world usage Older benchmarks like SWE-bench Pro suffer from data contamination and high grading errors, including a 24% false negative rate In contrast, DeepSWE uses entirely original, handcrafted challenges across 91 repositories and 5 programming languages It features concise, behavior-focused prompts that require end-to-end repository exploration On the DeepSWE leaderboard, GPT-5.5 dominates with a 70% pass rate, outperforming Claude Opus 4.7 by over 15 points Furthermore, GPT-5.5 proves highly efficient, completing trials in 20 minutes at a cost of $5.80, compared to Opus 4.7 which takes 37 minutes and costs $16.00. http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6LwQ8RbU9as

slides.title: Anthropic's SRT (Sandbox Runtime) https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime Typescript orchestrates OS-level
slides.text: Anthropic's SRT (Sandbox Runtime) https://github.com/anthropic-experimental/sandbox-runtime Typescript orchestrates OS-level sandboxing On MacOS there is a sandbox-exec command line utility that lets you run any process under a strict security policy TypeScript can invoke it with proper Seatbelt profile (a Scheme-like DSL) The kernel then intercepts every system call - file access, network connections, process forks - and enforces the policy across the entire process tree, including subprocesses For network filtering, SRT runs a local HTTP/SOCKS5 proxy. The Seatbelt profile blocks all direct outbound connections; traffic must route through the proxy, which enforces the domain allowlist. On Linux, SRT uses bubblewrap with user namespaces instead https://github.com/containers/bubblewrap In both cases, TypeScript's role is purely orchestration: generate the policy, start the proxy, and spawn the target process inside the sandbox.

slides.title: AI Updates Agent Compiler - Optimized Reusable Paths
slides.text: AI Updates Agent Compiler - Optimized Reusable Paths "Your AI Agent Is Wasting Time Thinking" - by Sumant Thakur https://sumantthakur.substack.com/p/the-agent-compiler-is-coming Core Idea: The Agent Compiler Current AI agents are essentially "chatbots with tools", they re-reason from scratch every time they encounter a task. This is inefficient An "agent compiler" would transform an agent's learned experiences and reasoning patterns into optimized, reusable execution paths, so agents stop wasting compute re-thinking things they've already figured out From: Interpret → execute (current state: reasoning at runtime every time) To: Compile → execute (distilling learned patterns into faster, cheaper, more reliable execution) The implication is significant for production AI systems: agents that "compile" their workflows could be dramatically more efficient, consistent, and cost-effective at scale Rather than burning tokens re-deliberating on solved problems, they'd run pre-optimized paths, making agentic AI less experimental and more industrial-grade Google DeepMind - Alpha Proof Nexus AI framework for autonomously solving open math problems Unlike traditional language models that hallucinate, this system connects frontier AI with Lean, a formal proof assistant that mechanically verifies mathematical reasoning step-by-step Through a continuous loop of generating code, reading error messages, and adjusting its approach, the system independently solved nine open Erdős problems - including two that remained unsolved for over 56 years - along with 44 open conjectures Remarkably, these breakthroughs cost only a few hundred dollars in computing power per problem This milestone proves AI can discover entirely new human knowledge, promising to dramatically accelerate future scientific progress across physics, chemistry, and medicine. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MgiJ5C1pQBg

slides.title: Anthropic "When AI builds itself" paper Anthropic "When
slides.text: Anthropic "When AI builds itself" paper Anthropic "When AI builds itself" paper https://www.anthropic.com/institute/recursive-self-improvement Matthew Berman https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a56T6OQtwEg Recursive self-improvement (RSI) in AI development - AI systems are increasingly being used to design and develop their own successors Human role is transitioning from writing code to prompting, verifying, and setting research direction The bottleneck shifts from code writing to code verifying Inside Anthropic, most of the code is written by AI. AI is significantly accelerating the speed at which tasks are completed Three possible futures: (1) Trend Stalls, (2) Tren continues, but humans remain in the loop for direction and judgment, (3) Full RSI - AI systems autonomously build their own successors, leading to an intelligence explosion Berman also provides commentary on Anthropic’s "fear-based marketing" strategy, noting that while the company advocates for slowing down the development of frontier AI to ensure safety, their current internal reliance on powerful, unreleased models (like the "Mythos" preview) suggests they are highly motivated to maintain their competitive lead

slides.title: Ray Kurzweil with Peter H. Diamandis on Moonshots
slides.text: Ray Kurzweil with Peter H. Diamandis on Moonshots Ray Kurzweil with Peter H. Diamandis on Moonshots Ray Kurzweil reaffirmed his long-standing prediction of AGI by 2029, citing continued exponential growth in computing and recent advances in large language models He argues AI already outperforms humans in some domains, including medical diagnosis, and will reach vastly higher intelligence levels by the 2045 singularity The discussion highlighted debates around AI consciousness and personhood, with no clear scientific definition but growing practical relevance Kurzweil and others emphasized that education systems are outdated, as AI can teach content while universities primarily provide socialization Economically, society is unprepared for post-scarcity shifts Kurzweil ultimately emphasized the transformative power of technology to scale access, turning expensive innovations into universally available tools

slides.title: Context Chain-of-Thought - Context-CoT "Context-CoT: Enhancing Context Learning
slides.text: Context Chain-of-Thought - Context-CoT "Context-CoT: Enhancing Context Learning via High-Quality Reasoning Synthesis" - https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25354 Unlike standard in-context learning, which simply activates existing parametric knowledge, context learning requires models to internalize entirely unfamiliar or contradictory rules provided exclusively within a prompt Testing reveals that frontier models fail massively on these real-world tasks because teacher LLMs are "lazy," generating flawed, post-hoc rationalizations based on pre-training memory rather than the new rules Context-CoT solves this by hiding the final answers from teacher models during data synthesis and optimizing step-wise reasoning to minimize cognitive friction for smaller student models Implementing this approach yields a noticeable performance jump on difficult context benchmarks https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9ngD_BKKtek Huawei Semiconductor "Tau (τ) Scaling" New chip design - https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l5RZOy_tqYw New Metric (Tau Scaling) - instead of focusing on shrinking the physical transistor, Tau scaling optimizes signal travel time "tau" - the time it takes for electrical pulses to move between components Tau scaling seeks to optimize the "corridors" rather than shrinking the "rooms" Logic Folding - folding circuit elements vertically in 3D space - placing frequently communicating components next to each other, dramatically slashing travel latency and boosting overall chip efficiency Huawei was using this approach over the last several years, including Huawei Mate 60 Pro smartphone and their Ascend 910C AI accelerator The upcoming Kirin chip (expected Autumn 2026) will be the first commercial product to fully deploy the finalized logic folding architecture

slides.title: "The AI Layoff Trap" Paper "The AI Layoff
slides.text: "The AI Layoff Trap" Paper "The AI Layoff Trap" Paper - https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.20617 The paper argues that rational firms can get trapped in an automation arms race that displaces workers beyond what is collectively optimal, ultimately harming both workers and firm owners by eroding consumer demand It also concludes that only a Pigouvian automation tax (rather than UBI, upskilling, or capital taxes) can effectively correct this market failure A Pigouvian tax (named after early 20th-century economist Arthur Pigou ) is a tax levied on any market activity that generates negative externalities - costs borne by third parties not involved in the transaction The canonical example is a carbon tax : a firm burning fossil fuels imposes climate costs on society, so the tax forces the firm to "internalize" those societal costs, making its private costs align with the true social costs. An automation tax would charge firms per worker displaced by AI or robotics, thus forcing companies to weigh the full social cost of automation, not just the private cost comparison between human wages and AI subscriptions The paper argues other commonly proposed remedies fall short: UBI — redistributes after the damage is done, doesn't change firm incentives Upskilling/retraining — too slow relative to the pace of AI displacement Capital gains taxes — target profits broadly, not the specific externality Arthur Cecil Pigou (1877-1959)
